text:
Alex G: quick check — i saw something weird combining stop sequences and max_tokens on hosted API. example payload:
```
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model": "redwood-3-small",
  "prompt": "Q: Translate this to french:\nHello world\n",
  "max_tokens": 6,
  "stop": ["\n\n"],
  "temperature": 0.7,
  "top_p": 0.9,
  "logprobs": 5
}
```
Behavior: when the stop appears inside a partial token, the response truncates but `logprobs` array is empty. is that expected? cc @Marta

Marta: iirc stop should win over max_tokens. but logprobs being empty feels like a bug. can you paste the raw streaming frames or the event log?

Alex G: pasted raw frames in the gist link (https://internal.gists/4523) — gist shows streaming frames: text chunks, then final `done` frame; final frame has no `logprobs` object even though earlier tokens had them.

Samir: fwiw we shipped a tiny change to streaming flush logic in last canary that might affect this. short version: to avoid double-tokenizing on the hot path we skip recomputing probs if we early-truncate for stops.

Samir: so current behavior is somewhat by design, but it's surprising. we should clarify docs or change runtime.

Ryan: observed a related quirk on dedicated: if top_p < 1 and temperature > 0 the tokenizer sampling path can split tokens differently, which combined with stop matching mid-token, leads to an empty `logprobs` payload. minimal repro: prompt "The quick brown fox" with stop ["fox"] and max_tokens 2 — streaming result differs between hosts.

Alex G: ok — proposal: treat `logprobs` as best-effort when termination is caused by `stop`. update contract to say it may be omitted if truncation happens mid-token or before final logprob pass.

Marta: agreed. i'll draft a short note for the API docs: "When a stop sequence causes early termination, token-level `logprobs` and token offsets are best-effort and may be absent if termination occurs mid-token or prior to finalization. Clients that require token-level probs should either avoid stop-only termination or request a post-hoc scoring endpoint."

Samir: another option: runtime attempts a final light tokenization pass only in the stop-only path to populate `logprobs`. perf impact should be measured. i'll add perf numbers to the GH issue.

Alex G: created GH issue #4523 with repro, gist, and perf notes. linking: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/4523

Marta: thanks. @deploy-bot did the canary that touched streaming get rolled back?

deploy-bot: canary rollback completed at 2026-03-17T15:12Z — affected hosts 3/12. logs: https://ci.internal/reports/4523

Ryan: i'll add a unit/regression test to the api-contract suite asserting that `logprobs` may be absent when stop triggers mid-token (so we don't break clients by flipping the guarantee).

Alex G: sounds good. marking this thread as resolved for now — we'll follow up if Samir's perf numbers make the finalization pass feasible. thanks all :thumbsup:
